chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Awadd al-Ta'i, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who marries a woman but does not have what he can give her [as dowry], so he enters into her [consummates the marriage]. He said, 'There is no harm; it is merely a debt upon him for her.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible
key_terms.مَهْر: Dowry given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry and consummate the marriage if he cannot pay the dowry immediately?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the absence of immediate funds for the dowry (mahr) does not invalidate the marriage contract or the right to consummation. The unpaid amount is legally classified as a debt (dayn) upon the husband, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that mahr is a right of the wife that can be deferred, thereby facilitating marriage even for those with limited means.
